the presence of Pl-A2 allele of GPIIa β-subunit is associated with the increased risk of acute coronary insuﬁciency.
the Pl-A(2)/Pl-A(3) allele combination is associated with a higher incidence of progressive angina and myocardium infarction in comparison with the Pl-A(I) homozygotes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of the Pl-A2 allele of the PlA(II) gene is associated with a more severe course of acute coronary events.
the Pl-A(III) allele is associated with a higher incidence of myocardial infarctions in patients with unstable angina pectoris, but with a lower incidence in those with acute myocardial infarct.
the clinical course of patients with the Pl-A(2) genotype is more severe and complicated than that of patients with the normal Pl-A(1) allele.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients carrying the Pl-A(2/2) genotype are more prone to develop progressive angina than patients homozygote for Pl-A(1/1) or Pl-A(2) allele.
the presence of the Pl-A(I) genotype of the GPIIIa β-chain in patients with acute coronary insuffi-ciency is associated with a more severe clinical course of this pathology.
